activities.title: Daily money check-in
activities.desc: A calm 2-minute look at today's money — no judgment, just awareness.
activities.value: Builds the habit of looking at your money regularly, the single strongest predictor of better decisions.
activities.take: Awareness first. You can't steer what you don't look at.

activities.title: One-minute lesson: needs vs wants
activities.desc: A bite-sized lesson on separating essentials from nice-to-haves.
activities.value: Gives you a simple filter for everyday spending decisions.

lesson.b: Needs keep life running — rent, food, transport, bills, minimum debt payments. Wants make life nicer — dining out, upgrades, subscriptions. Many purchases are a mix: a phone is a need, the newest model is a want. The goal isn't to remove wants; it's to choose them on purpose.

q.why: Utilities keep your home running. The others can be planned for deliberately.

activities.take: Choose your wants on purpose, and your needs are always covered first.

activities.title: Quick financial quiz
activities.desc: Three questions on everyday money concepts.
activities.value: Retrieval practice makes financial concepts stick far better than reading.

lesson.b: When earnings are reinvested, you earn on your earnings. Over long periods this snowball effect is powerful — which is why starting early with small amounts often matters more than starting late with big ones. (Illustration only: returns are never guaranteed.)

q.why: Time in the market and regular contributions matter more than perfect timing.

activities.take: Time + consistency beat timing.

activities.title: Spending awareness challenge
activities.desc: Review last month's top spending categories and spot one thing to adjust.
activities.value: Most people can't name their top 3 spending categories — knowing them unlocks easy savings.
items: Picked one category to trim by 5%
activities.take: Small targeted trims beat broad restriction.

activities.title: Savings micro-challenge
activities.desc: Set a tiny automatic transfer to a goal — then see its yearly effect.
activities.value: Automation removes willpower from saving.

lesson.b: Instead of saving what's left after spending, move a fixed amount to savings right after income arrives. Even ₹1,000 a month becomes ₹12,000 a year before any growth — and the habit scales as income grows.

q.q: What's the key benefit of automating savings?
q.why: Automation makes saving the default instead of a decision you re-make every month.

activities.take: Make saving the default.

activities.title: Financial wellness check
activities.desc: Rate six areas of your financial life in under four minutes.
activities.value: A regular self-check shows where attention actually helps.
items: Debt: I know what I owe and the cost
Investing: I have a plan for long-term money
Goals: I know my top 3 goals
Emergency: I know how many months I could cover
activities.take: Unchecked boxes are your next focus areas, not failures.

activities.title: Investing concept: diversification
activities.desc: Why not putting everything in one place can reduce the damage of any single surprise.
activities.value: Helps you spot concentration risk in your own plan.

lesson.b: Different assets behave differently in different conditions. Spreading money across them doesn't prevent losses, but it can reduce how much any one event hurts. How you spread depends on goals, time horizon and comfort with ups and downs — it's personal, not universal.

q.q: What does diversification mainly aim to reduce?
q.why: It reduces dependence on any single asset or event; it can't remove risk.

activities.take: Spread risk, don't chase certainty.

activities.title: Personal goal review
activities.desc: Look at each goal's progress and confirm it's still the right target.
activities.value: Goals drift; a quick review keeps your money pointed at what matters.
items: Confirmed target dates still make sense
Chose which goal gets the next ₹ I save
activities.take: Goals are living plans. Reviewing them is the plan.

activities.title: Check your emergency fund
activities.desc: How many months of essentials could you cover today?
activities.value: The emergency fund is the foundation every other goal stands on.

lesson.b: An emergency fund is money set aside only for surprises — job gaps, medical bills, urgent repairs. Common guidance is 3–6 months of essential expenses, more if income is uneven or others depend on you. Keep it easy to reach and low-risk.

q.q: Where should emergency money mainly prioritise?
q.why: You need it available when something goes wrong, so access and safety come first.

activities.take: Emergency money's job is availability, not returns.

activities.title: Understand your risk profile
activities.desc: A short reflection on how you feel about ups and downs.
activities.value: Aligning investments with your real comfort level helps you stay invested.

lesson.b: Tolerance is how comfortable you feel with ups and downs. Capacity is how much loss your finances can actually absorb. Good plans respect the lower of the two.

q.q: Your investments fall 15% in a month. Capacity-wise, what matters most?
o: Whether you need this money soon
q.why: If you need the money soon, a fall is far more damaging than if the horizon is long.

activities.take: Plan for the lower of tolerance and capacity.

activities.title: Weekly financial review
activities.desc: Ten-minute reset: income in, money out, goals moved.
activities.value: A weekly rhythm catches small problems before they grow.
items: Moved money to at least one goal
activities.take: Ten minutes a week can replace hours of month-end stress.

activities.title: Savings progress review
activities.desc: See which goals moved and which stalled.
activities.value: Visible progress keeps motivation honest.
items: Compared saved vs planned this week
activities.take: Adjust the plan, not your self-worth.

activities.title: Portfolio learning
activities.desc: One concept about how portfolios work — no trading required.
activities.value: Informed investors make calmer decisions.
items: Compared it to my simulated allocation
activities.take: Understanding first, action second.

activities.title: Debt management challenge
activities.desc: List debts by cost and plan the next extra payment.
activities.value: Targeting the costliest debt first saves the most interest.
items: Listed each debt with rate and EMI
Chose where any extra payment goes
activities.take: Cost, not size, decides the order.

activities.title: Insurance awareness
activities.desc: A concept walkthrough of what protection means for your situation.
activities.value: Protection gaps are invisible until they matter.
items: Listed who depends on my income
Noted what health and life cover I have
Flagged gaps to discuss with an advisor
activities.take: Protection protects every other goal.

activities.title: Financial knowledge assessment
activities.desc: A short quiz arena run to measure what you've learned.
activities.value: Shows learning growth over time.
activities.take: Knowledge compounds too.

activities.title: Monthly financial wrapped
activities.desc: Your month in a story — progress, learning, wins.
activities.value: Reflection turns activity into understanding.
activities.take: Celebrate verified progress.

activities.title: Financial wellness assessment
activities.desc: A deeper six-dimension check-in.
activities.value: The most honest picture of where you stand.
activities.take: Measure, then improve.

activities.title: Goal progress report
activities.desc: Each goal: saved, pace, projected date range.
activities.value: Shows whether today's pace still reaches tomorrow's goal.
activities.take: Pace is the plan.

activities.title: Financial habits analysis
activities.desc: Which habits helped, which didn't, and which to keep.
activities.value: Habits, not events, change outcomes.
items: Noted my best habit this month
activities.take: Keep what works. Fix one thing.

activities.title: Personalised improvement plan
activities.desc: A simple three-step plan for next month.
activities.value: Turns insight into action.
activities.take: Three small actions beat one big intention.
